TRANSFORMER · ILLUSTRATED OVERVIEW

Words become vectors. Attention connects their meaning.

A Transformer models token relationships through attention and learned layers, enabling language understanding and sequence generation.

01 · CORE IDEA

How one token can combine context from a whole sentence

Attention gives each position a way to use relevant tokens; positional information helps the network distinguish sequence order.
questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: B. Transformer ముందుగా Tokensని Numerical Vectorsగా Represent చేస్తుంది. Self-Attention ద్వారా ఒక Tokenకి Usefulగా ఉండే ఇతర Tokens నుంచి Information తీసుకుంటుంది. Positional Information వల్ల Word Order కూడా తెలుస్తుంది. అందుకే Translation, Classification, Text Generation వంటి Tasks చేయగలదు.

02 · WHY TRANSFORMERS

Compare chained recurrence with parallel attention

LSTMs improve memory of earlier signals, but their recurrence still links computations across timesteps. Transformers allow parallel training across sequence positions.
questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: D. RNN, LSTMలో Next Step, Previous Step Calculationపై Depend అవుతుంది. కాబట్టి Parallel Trainingకి Limit ఉంటుంది; Long-Range Relationships నేర్చుకోవడం కష్టమవచ్చు. Transformer Self-Attentionతో Distant Tokensని Directగా Connect చేసి, Trainingలో Sequence Positionsపై Calculations Parallelగా చేయగలదు.

Input Sentenceని Tokenize చేయకముందే Final Predictionsని ముందుగానే Generate చేస్తుంది.

03 · INPUT TO OUTPUT

Follow tokens through five different computations

Actual Transformer stacks repeat attention and feed-forward layers. Depending on the task, final predictions may represent tokens, classes, or an output sequence.
questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Input Textని Token IDsగా Convert చేస్తాం. ప్రతి Token IDకి Embedding Vector వస్తుంది; Position Information కూడా Add అవుతుంది. Attention, Feed-Forward Layers ఆ Informationని Process చేసి Contextual Representations Build చేస్తాయి. Final Output Head Token Predictions లేదా Task-specific Output Generate చేస్తుంది.

Decoder Cross-Attention, Encoder Representationsని Ignore చేసి Future Tokensని Directగా Read చేస్తుంది.
Encoder, Decoder Blocks Attention, Residuals, Normalization, Feed-Forward Layersని Combine చేస్తాయి.
Query, Key, Value Projectionsని Final Softmax Results వచ్చిన తర్వాత మాత్రమే Compute చేస్తారు.

04 · ORIGINAL TRANSFORMER

Trace encoder memory, decoder masking, Q/K/V and cross-attention

In the original 2017 Transformer, positional encodings enter the stacks, residual-plus-normalization wraps each sublayer, and the decoder's self-attention is causally masked.
questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: C. Original Transformer Encoderలో Self-Attention, Feed-Forward Sub-layers ఉంటాయి. Decoderలో Masked Self-Attention, Encoder–Decoder Cross-Attention, Feed-Forward Layers ఉంటాయి. ప్రతి Attention Head, Q/K/V Projections ఉపయోగించి Scaled Dot-Product Attention Compute చేస్తుంది. Residual Connections, Layer Normalization, Position Information, Masks కూడా Key Parts.

05 · PYTORCH WALKTHROUGH

Read the manual attention implementation next to a tensor-flow map

● ● ● tiny_transformer.py · executable PyTorch
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class TinyTransformer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab=32, d=32, h=4):
        super().__init__()
        self.d, self.h = d, h
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab, d)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(64, d)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d, 3*d)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(d, d)
        self.ff = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(d, 4*d),
                                nn.GELU(), nn.Linear(4*d, d))
        self.ln1, self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d), nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.readout = nn.Linear(d, vocab)

    def forward(self, ids):
        b, t = ids.shape
        x = self.embed(ids) + self.pos(
            torch.arange(t, device=ids.device))
        q, k, v = self.qkv(x).reshape(
            b, t, 3, self.h, self.d//self.h
        ).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        scores = q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)
        scores = scores / (self.d//self.h)**0.5
        future = torch.ones(t, t, device=ids.device,
            dtype=torch.bool).triu(1)
        weights = scores.masked_fill(
            future, -torch.inf).softmax(-1)
        a = (weights @ v).transpose(1, 2)
        a = a.reshape(b, t, self.d)
        x = self.ln1(x + self.proj(a))
        x = self.ln2(x + self.ff(x))
        return self.readout(x)

model = TinyTransformer()
opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
tokens = torch.randint(0, 32, (4, 9))
for _ in range(3):  # Toy demonstration data
    x, y = tokens[:, :-1], tokens[:, 1:]
    logits = model(x)
    loss = F.cross_entropy(
        logits.reshape(-1, 32), y.reshape(-1))
    opt.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    opt.step()
print(f"Loss: {loss.item():.3f}")

The example uses random tokens only to demonstrate a real forward/backward pass, not language proficiency.

Q/K/V are computed explicitly, split across heads, masked before Softmax, then combined with residual and feed-forward layers. The short loop trains on next-token cross entropy.
questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: B. First Token Embeddings, Position Embeddings Add చేస్తాం. Next Q/K/V Project చేసి Multiple Headsగా Split చేస్తాం. Future Tokens కనిపించకుండా Causal Maskని Softmaxకు ముందు Apply చేస్తాం. Residual, Normalization, Feed-Forward Blocks Process చేస్తాయి. Cross-Entropy Loss ఆధారంగా Backpropagation, Optimizer Model Weightsని Train చేస్తాయి. Diagramలో Code Toy Tokensతో Demonstration మాత్రమే.

06 · THREE ARCHITECTURES

Compare bidirectional, causal and encoder–decoder attention

BERT typically learns masked-token representations, GPT learns autoregressive predictions, and T5 trains text-to-text objectives with cross-attention.
questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: D. BERT Encoder-only Model; Bidirectional Self-Attentionతో Masked Language Modeling వంటి Tasks చేస్తుంది. GPT Decoder-only Model; Causal Maskతో Autoregressive Next-Token Prediction చేస్తుంది. T5 Encoder–Decoder Architecture; Encoder Inputని Represent చేస్తుంది, Decoder Cross-Attentionతో Inputపై Focus చేసి Text Generate చేస్తుంది.

questions.stem: Transformersని Large Language Models (LLMs)గా Scale చేస్తే Quadratic Attention Cost, Long Context, KV-cache Memory, Training Instability, Inference Latency Problems ఎందుకు వస్తాయి? FlashAttention, GQA, RoPE, Sparse Attention, Distributed Training ఎలా Help చేస్తాయి?
options: Tiled Attention Memory Traffic తగ్గిస్తుంది; Shared KV Heads Cache తగ్గిస్తాయి; Distributed Training Work Split చేస్తుంది.
RoPE అన్ని Attention Calculations Eliminate చేస్తుంది; Sparse Attention ఎప్పుడూ Exact Dense Results ఇస్తుంది.
Context Length పెరిగితే Compute Cost Automatically తగ్గి Training Problems అన్నీ Resolve అవుతాయి.
Multiple GPUs వాడితే Large KV Cache ఉన్నా Inference Latency Completely Disappear అవుతుంది.
questions.explanation: Simple Explanation: Conversation Longగా ఉంటే Attentionకి More Compute, Memory అవసరం. FlashAttention, GQA, Distributed Training వంటి Techniques ఈ Costs Reduce చేయడంలో Help చేస్తాయి.
questions.figure:
07 · PRODUCTION LLM BOTTLENECKS

See where memory grows and how optimization techniques respond

FlashAttention cuts attention memory I/O; GQA shrinks K/V caches; RoPE supplies relative position behavior; sparse attention changes connectivity; distributed training splits work. The trade-offs depend on workload.
questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Dense Self-Attentionలో Tokens పెరిగినప్పుడు Pairwise Interactions Quadraticగా Grow అవుతాయి. FlashAttention Tilingతో Memory I/O Reduce చేస్తుంది. GQA, Fewer Shared K/V Heads ద్వారా KV Cache Size తగ్గిస్తుంది. RoPE Relative Position Behaviorని Support చేస్తుంది. Sparse Attention కొన్ని Links మాత్రమే Compute చేస్తుంది. Distributed Training GPUs మధ్య Work Divide చేస్తుంది. ఇవేవీ అన్ని Problemsని ఒకేసారి Solve చేయవు.
